body:
Today is a quiet day for gold arbitrage. The scanner surfaced exactly one cross-platform opportunity: buying Yes on Polymarket's Will Gold (XAUUSD) hit (HIGH) $4,700 in August? at 7.9 cents while buying No on Kalshi's Gold price on August 31, 2026 — Above $4731.99 at 91 cents, for a combined cost of 98.9 cents against a guaranteed $1 payout. After fees that nets just over half a cent per contract, and the order books only support about 100 contracts — a total capturable profit of 53 cents. That's not a trading idea, it's a rounding artifact: the two contracts aren't measuring the same thing. Polymarket's is a touch market, meaning it pays out the moment gold's intraday price ever crosses $4,700 during August, while Kalshi's is a settle market, paying out based only on the official spot price at a single snapshot, 5:00 PM EDT on August 31. A touch above $4,700 sometime this month doesn't guarantee the month-end settle price finishes below $4,731.99 or vice versa, so the two legs aren't a true hedge despite the numbers lining up neatly on paper.

Elsewhere, pricing across both venues looks internally consistent and unremarkable. Kalshi's step-ladder of settle contracts implies the market currently sees gold's month-end value somewhere in the low-to-mid $4,300s, with the $4,331.99 strike priced near 63-72 cents and the $4,411.99 strike near even money. Polymarket's weekly touch contracts tell a similar story, with the $4,450 high-touch contract trading around 72-76 cents. The single-day directional contract for August 18 is priced almost exactly at 50/50 (49-51 cents), which is typical for a coin-flip-style short-term contract and not indicative of any unusual sentiment. Nothing in today's data points to a large price move or a liquidity gap worth flagging.
headline: Gold's only cross-platform arbitrage today is a mismatch, not a real trade
